seoTitle: Belfast cruise port guide: shuttle, Titanic and City Hall
seoDescription: Belfast Cruise Terminal is 6 km from City Hall; shuttle or taxi about 20 min, no walking route. Titanic Belfast £24.95 online (2026). Back 90 min early.
quickAnswer: Ships berth at the Belfast Cruise Terminal (D1) inside the working harbour estate, about 6 km and 20 minutes by road from City Hall; there is no pedestrian route out, so you leave by shuttle, taxi or tour. The shuttle drops at the Visit Belfast Welcome Centre beside City Hall, and your cruise line decides whether it is free. Be back at the shuttle stop 90 minutes before all-aboard.
intro: Belfast is the busiest cruise port on the island of Ireland, with 141 calls scheduled for 2026. The cruise terminal sits deep in an industrial harbour estate, so the day starts with a 20-minute ride to City Hall. From there the centre is compact and walkable: City Hall, St George's Market and the Titanic Quarter are all within about half an hour on foot. Titanic Belfast is the big draw and uses timed tickets, so book ahead. The Giant's Causeway is about an hour and a half each way by road, which makes it a full-day trip. Belfast Harbour is building a £90m deepwater cruise quay at the mouth of the port, due in 2028.

terminals.name: Belfast Cruise Terminal (D1)
terminals.notes: 20 Airport Road West, inside the Belfast Harbour estate. Opened in 2019 as the first dedicated cruise terminal on the island of Ireland. 480 m berth. Visitor information desk staffed by Visit Belfast, gift shop, internet access and a taxi rank. City Hall is about 3.8 miles (6.1 km), around 20 minutes by road.

terminals.name: Stormont Wharf and Pollock Dock
terminals.notes: Stormont Wharf has been used for smaller ships and Pollock Dock for turnaround calls. Your cruise documents will name the berth; use the shuttle or a taxi from either.

walkability.detail: The terminal is inside a working harbour estate with no pedestrian route to the city. Take the shuttle, a taxi or a tour. Once in the centre, it is easy on foot: City Hall to Titanic Belfast takes about 25–30 minutes.

transportSections.mode: Cruise shuttle to the Visit Belfast Welcome Centre
transportSections.cost: Free or charged depending on your cruise line; check your daily programme (2026)
transportSections.detail: Drops at the Visit Belfast Welcome Centre, 9 Donegall Square North, beside City Hall. Shuttle times are posted in the cruise terminal. The Welcome Centre has tourist information, tour and transport tickets, free Wi-Fi and a freephone for taxis.

transportSections.cost: Metered or quoted; confirm before setting off
transportSections.time: About 20 min to City Hall; about 9 min to Titanic Belfast
transportSections.detail: Rank at the terminal. Value Cabs can be called on 028 9080 9080, and there is a freephone in the terminal and at the Welcome Centre.

transportSections.mode: Glider G2 (city centre to Titanic Quarter)
transportSections.detail: Leaves from Wellington Place by Donegall Square North. Useful if you take the shuttle to City Hall and want to ride rather than walk to Titanic Belfast.

transportSections.time: 25–30 min City Hall to Titanic Belfast
transportSections.detail: The centre is compact. St George's Market is near Belfast Central station, opposite the Waterfront Hall.

transportSections.mode: Ship tour or coach tour to the Giant's Causeway
transportSections.time: About 1.5 hours each way; 8–9 hours door to door
transportSections.detail: About 60 miles from the terminal along the Causeway Coastal Route. Day tours also leave from City Hall and can be booked through Visit Belfast.

returnTiming.rule: Be at the shuttle stop at the Visit Belfast Welcome Centre 90 minutes before all-aboard (16:00 for a 17:30 all-aboard). If you go to the Giant's Causeway independently, leave the Causeway at least three hours before all-aboard.
returnTiming.detail: The ride from City Hall to the terminal takes about 20 minutes and city traffic in the late afternoon can slow it. Shuttle queues build in the last hour. You cannot walk back to the ship, so do not count on getting a taxi at the last minute on a busy afternoon.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: Take a taxi straight to the Belfast Cruise Terminal on Airport Road West; it is about 20 minutes from the centre. If you will miss all-aboard, call the port agent number on your daily programme straight away.

excursionAdvice: Belfast city is easy to do independently once the shuttle drops you at City Hall: Titanic Belfast, the City Hall tour, St George's Market and the Ulster Museum are all in or close to the centre. The ship's tour earns its price for the Giant's Causeway and the Causeway Coastal Route, which take about an hour and a half each way and 8–9 hours in all, leaving little margin on a normal call. A guided city tour is also worth considering if you want the political murals and Troubles history explained.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship docks at the Belfast Cruise Terminal at 08:00 and all-aboard is 17:30, on a Saturday from May to September.

steps.what: Shuttle from the terminal to the Visit Belfast Welcome Centre at City Hall, about 20 minutes.
Pick up a map at the Welcome Centre, then walk 25–30 minutes to the Titanic Quarter, or take the Glider G2 from Wellington Place.
Titanic Belfast on a pre-booked timed ticket (£24.95 online, 2026). Allow 2–3 hours.
Taxi or walk to St George's Market for lunch from the Saturday food stalls (open until 15:00).
Belfast City Hall guided tour (£6, card only, tickets at reception on the day; Saturday tours at 12:00, 14:00 and 15:00 from May to September).
Free time around Donegall Square and the shopping streets.
Shuttle back from the Welcome Centre, 90 minutes before all-aboard.
Back on board, an hour before all-aboard.

sights.name: Titanic Belfast
sights.why: The Titanic story in the Titanic Quarter, beside the Harland and Wolff shipyard, with the SS Nomadic nearby.
sights.tip: Timed entry; book in advance, especially in summer. Hours vary by season; on the day checked in October 2026 it opened 08:50–17:45 with last admission at 15:50.

sights.name: Belfast City Hall
sights.why: The city's civic building on Donegall Square, next to the shuttle stop.
sights.cost: £6 adult, children free with a ticket (2026)
sights.tip: Tours May to September on weekdays at 11:00, 14:00, 15:00 and 16:00, Saturdays at 12:00, 14:00 and 15:00. Tickets are first come, first served at reception, card or contactless only. Arrive 15 minutes early; late arrivals are not admitted.

sights.name: St George's Market
sights.why: Victorian covered market built 1890–1896, with food, crafts and antiques stalls.
sights.tip: Open Friday 08:00–14:00, Saturday 09:00–15:00 and Sunday 10:00–15:00 only. Saturday is the food and craft market.

sights.name: Ulster Museum
sights.why: Art, natural history and local history, including Girona Armada gold, the mummy Takabuti and the Troubles gallery.
sights.tip: In the Botanic Gardens about a mile south of the centre. Open Tuesday to Sunday 10:00–17:00, closed Mondays except bank holidays. Metro 8 and 8A stop nearby.

sights.name: Crumlin Road Gaol
sights.why: Former prison tour with the tunnel to the courthouse, the wings and the execution cell.
sights.cost: Check prices when booking; cheaper online
sights.tip: Open daily, first tour 10:00, last at about 16:30. The tunnel and drop cell are not wheelchair accessible.

sights.name: Botanic Gardens
sights.why: City park beside the Ulster Museum.

sights.name: Giant's Causeway
sights.why: The famous rock columns on the north coast.
sights.cost: Visitor Experience tickets via the official site; shuttle bus at the site £1
sights.tip: About 1.5 hours each way from the terminal. The coastline is open at all times; the Visitor Experience opened 09:00–17:00 (last admission 16:00) in October 2026. Best done on a ship or coach tour.

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning to walk from the ship into Belfast.
commonMistakes.fix: There is no pedestrian route out of the harbour estate. Use the shuttle, a taxi or a tour.

commonMistakes.mistake: Turning up at Titanic Belfast without a ticket.
commonMistakes.fix: Entry is timed and summer slots fill. Book online, which is also £2 cheaper for adults.

commonMistakes.mistake: Trying to fit the Giant's Causeway in on your own on a short call.
commonMistakes.fix: It is about 1.5 hours each way and a full day in total. Take the ship's tour or a coach tour, or stay in the city.

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning St George's Market on a weekday.
commonMistakes.fix: It opens Friday to Sunday only.

commonMistakes.mistake: Paying cash for the City Hall tour.
commonMistakes.fix: Tickets are card or contactless only and sold on the day at reception.

safety: Belfast city centre and the Titanic Quarter are busy and generally safe for visitors; take normal city precautions with bags and phones. The harbour estate is an industrial area: stay on the shuttle or in a taxi and keep out of operational zones. Political murals and memorials are part of the city's history; a guided tour is the easiest way to visit them with context.
accessibility: The terminal has space for coaches, shuttles and taxis at the door. Ask your cruise line whether the shuttle is wheelchair accessible. The City Hall tour is accessible, but the route is on the first floor, and visitors who cannot evacuate without a lift need a Personal Emergency Evacuation Plan. At Crumlin Road Gaol the tunnel and drop cell are not wheelchair accessible. The Giant's Causeway site offers an accessible shuttle, wheelchair hire and a Changing Places toilet.
rainyDay: Belfast has plenty indoors. Spend the morning at Titanic Belfast, then the free Ulster Museum or a City Hall tour. On Friday to Sunday, St George's Market is covered. Crumlin Road Gaol is another indoor option; wear warm clothing.
crowdTips: Belfast expects 141 cruise calls in 2026, and the largest ships can bring up to 6,000 passengers and crew. Titanic Belfast is the first stop for most visitors, so book an early timed slot or go after lunch. City Hall tours are first come, first served at reception, so buy tickets early in the day on big-ship days.

faqs.q: Is Belfast cruise port walkable to the city centre?
faqs.a: No. The terminal is about 6 km from City Hall inside a working harbour estate with no pedestrian route out. Take the shuttle or a taxi, about 20 minutes.

faqs.q: Is the Belfast cruise shuttle free?
faqs.a: It depends on your cruise line, which decides whether to charge. Check your daily programme. It drops at the Visit Belfast Welcome Centre beside City Hall.

faqs.q: How do I get from Belfast cruise port to Titanic Belfast?
faqs.a: A taxi takes about 9 minutes. Or take the shuttle to City Hall and walk 25–30 minutes, or ride the Glider G2 from Wellington Place.
£24.95 per adult online or £26.95 walk-up in 2026, with timed entry. Book ahead in summer.

faqs.q: Can I visit the Giant's Causeway from a Belfast cruise?
faqs.a: Yes, but it is about 1.5 hours each way and 8–9 hours door to door. A ship or coach tour is the safer choice.

faqs.q: What can I do in Belfast in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Titanic Belfast, a City Hall tour, St George's Market (Friday to Sunday) and the free Ulster Museum.
No. Ships berth at the Belfast Cruise Terminal (D1) or other berths in the harbour.

faqs.q: Is Belfast safe for cruise passengers?
faqs.a: Yes. Take normal city precautions and stay on the shuttle or in a taxi inside the harbour estate.
